boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Rutherford's Farm record (July 20, 1864) in Early's Raid and Operations Against the B&O Railroad [June-August 1864]. The July 19 skirmishes near Darkesville and the July 21-22 withdrawal to Strasburg are context. Campaign-wide marches, levies, captures, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads Divisions (5,850 total); the live field reads zero and the frozen side bounds are blank. Averell says he marched with Duval's infantry brigade, 1,350 strong, and 1,000 cavalry, joined by about 300 of the Second Virginia, and that the enemy engaged, Ramseur's infantry division and three cavalry brigades, was in all about 5,000. Pond gives Averell 2,350 men, about 2,700 with the Second Virginia, and says he was still numerically inferior.
claims.rationale: Averell's enemy figure is an interested estimate; the frozen 5,850's basis and side split are not established. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. Averell says the enemy was thrown into confusion and driven toward Winchester; Pond says Averell refrained from occupying Winchester. NPS says Early then withdrew to Fisher's Hill; Pond says he went to Middletown and on July 22 to Strasburg.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The withdrawal is campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,100 total; the live field reads 742 (US 242; CS 500). Averell gives the enemy 73 killed and 130 wounded left on the field and 17 officers and 250 men captured, with four guns, and his own loss as 53 killed, 155 wounded and 6 missing. Pond gives 203 Confederate killed and wounded, the same captures, a total Confederate loss probably more than 400, and Averell's loss as 214. NPS says nearly 300 men were captured.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Duval's, Shaw's and Coates's reports, Averell's itinerary and Rodes's September 12 letter (read, not selected; quoted by Pond) remain deferred; no Ramseur or Vaughn report was inspected.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office and field despatches; it quotes the reports of the commanders it describes and is not independent of them. Averell's July 28, 1864 report, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVII, Part 1, is one family of interested Union accounts. The Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
